sentences.english: The farmer has a small dog.
The dog loves the good farmer.
The farmer leads the dog into the field.
The dog guards the large field.
The farmer prepares water and food.
The dog takes the good food.
The dog sees a white bird.
And so the dog frightens the bird.
The farmer calls the faithful dog.
The dog is praised by the farmer.

sentences.latin: Magister noster pueros in scholam ducit.
sentences.english: Our teacher leads the boys into the school.
The teacher gives new books to the boys.

sentences.latin: Pueri verba magistri audiunt et libros aperiunt.
sentences.english: The boys hear the teacher's words and open the books.

sentences.latin: Magister puero parvo verba difficilia dat.
sentences.english: The teacher gives difficult words to the small boy.

sentences.latin: Puer magistro respondet, nam puer verba nova scit.
sentences.english: The boy answers the teacher, for the boy knows the new words.

sentences.latin: Itaque puer a magistro nostro laudatur.
sentences.english: And so the boy is praised by our teacher.

sentences.latin: Pueri verba magistri in libris suis scribunt.
sentences.english: The boys write the teacher's words in their own books.

sentences.latin: Magister libros puerorum videt et verba vera laudat.
sentences.english: The teacher sees the boys' books and praises the true words.

sentences.latin: Pueri magistrum sapientem amant, quod magister pueros monet.
sentences.english: The boys love the wise teacher, because the teacher advises the boys.

sentences.latin: Schola nostra a magistro fideli regitur.
sentences.english: Our school is ruled by the faithful teacher.

sentences.latin: Turris alta urbis veteris a militibus fortibus legionis nostrae custoditur.
sentences.english: The tall tower of the old city is guarded by the brave soldiers of our legion.
